playbook:
# My Playbook for ref_estate

**On property purchases:**

When I land on an unowned property, I will evaluate the purchase based on: (1) my current liquid cash position; (2) the rent income I'll collect over remaining laps; (3) how much cash I need to stay solvent for incoming rent payments. I will buy early properties aggressively when I have sufficient cushion, as they compound over 6 laps.

When I cannot afford a property without dropping below 40 liquid cash, I will pass. I learned this the hard way—my cash crunch in laps 4–6 forced me to skip the Mill despite it being valuable, and I finished with only 71 after already owning two properties. I should either buy more properties early when flush with cash, or be more selective about which properties I acquire.

**On cash tracking:**

When the bank tells me I've received transfers since my last turn, I will immediately add them to my declared balance before making any decision. I did this correctly on lap 5, but I need to stay disciplined about it every turn.

**On rent payments:**

When I owe rent, I will pay it first and calculate my new balance afterward. I will never try to buy property while owing rent.

**On final-lap decisions:**

When I'm on my last lap, I will not buy properties. By lap 6 there's no time to recoup the investment. I stayed disciplined on this.

**On salary passes:**

When I pass START, I will collect the salary immediately and add it to my declared balance. This is free cash and I should never miss it.

**General strategy revision:**

Looking at my score of 221, I accumulated the Wharf and Terrace but starved myself of cash in the middle laps. Next time, I should either: (1) buy more properties in laps 1–2 while I still have capital, or (2) be much more selective and only buy the highest-rent properties when I'm confident I can afford future rent obligations. A balanced portfolio of 3–4 properties with solid rent income beats owning 2 properties while staying cash-poor.
